title: Storage scenarios worksheet
subject: Computing
source: Seeded from computing/y9 lesson 7 (Storage scenarios worksheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: Memory and storage: RAM, ROM and secondary storage. To understand the different roles of RAM, ROM and secondary storage

questions.q: Why is the boot program stored in ROM, not RAM?
questions.a: ROM is non-volatile, so the start-up instructions are there when the power comes on.
questions.model: Teacher reasons: when the computer starts, RAM is empty because it is volatile; the CPU needs instructions at once, so they must be in non-volatile ROM.

questions.q: Which storage for a phone: HDD or SSD? Why?
questions.a: SSD: small, fast, no moving parts so it survives drops.

questions.q: Give one advantage of cloud storage.
questions.a: Access from any device; backed up off-site.

questions.q: Core: Choose storage for: a photographer's 4 TB archive; a pupil carrying homework; a school laptop. Justify each in the portal response box.
questions.a: HDD (cheap per GB, large); USB flash drive or OneDrive (portable); SSD (fast, robust).
questions.model: Teacher justifies the photographer: large capacity needed, cost matters more than speed, so HDD.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why adding RAM can make a computer faster.
questions.a: More programs and data fit in RAM, so less is swapped to slower secondary storage (virtual memory).

questions.q: Stretch: Compare SSD and HDD on speed, durability, capacity and cost.
questions.a: SSD faster and more durable; HDD larger and cheaper per gigabyte.

questions.q: ROM is... A) volatile B) non-volatile
Big question: why is unsaved work lost in a power cut?
questions.a: It is held in RAM, which is volatile.
